study type: Retrospective observational study using a nationwide registry
cohort: Singleton pregnant women registered in the Japanese nationwide perinatal registry database between 2013 and 2019.
finding: Fetomaternal hemorrhage (FMH) was significantly associated with fetal growth restriction and a single umbilical artery, and abnormal umbilical cord insertion was significantly associated with stillbirth or neonatal death among women with FMH.
followup_time: Up to 28 days post-birth (for neonatal death)
